title: Holding the Dirty Thing by the Clean Side

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The book distinguishes the capacity to enforce an order from its moral defensibility.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: A norm that changes no conduct has a different status from an operating institution.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Yet effective control alone cannot answer whether affected people are treated justly.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The text compares traditions that explain consent, procedure, recognition, order, and public justification.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Its own recurring test follows the distribution of costs through those accounts.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Readers can ask whether a justification remains credible from the weaker participant’s position.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: That question connects theoretical legitimacy to something observable in daily institutional life.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The full chapter preserves differences that a single definition of legitimacy would conceal.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The proposed social technologies begin by making costs and consequences more traceable.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: A burden ledger would describe where risk, stress, exposure, and lost opportunity go.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Contestability requires a usable route to explanation, appeal, correction, and representation.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: An attractive transparency interface would be insufficient if affected people cannot act on it.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The book also asks whether productivity gains reduce humiliation and unnecessary degradation.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: These are proposals for institutional testing, rather than a claim of completed implementation.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: Their value depends on making concealed transfers harder to maintain.

events.speaker: narrator
events.text: The reader can compare the proposals against organizations whose procedures are already familiar.
